artworks.title: La Brebis; Le Tandem
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: The image depicts two individuals on sepia-toned paper. The primary figure, a woman, is shown from the waist up facing slightly left with her right hand on her hip. Her facial features are outlined with attention to detail. She has light-colored hair in an updo and wears a large, detailed hat. She is in a jacket with large buttons and visible cuffs. The second figure, a man, is depicted from the chest up, possibly behind a window with shutters. He has facial hair and combed-back hair, wearing a dark outfit. The background includes foliage painted with loose strokes. Printed text on both sides mentions titles and names related to theater or literary works.

artworks.title: L'Inspecteur Général Revizor
artworks.medium: photorelief on wove paper
artworks.description: The image shows a drawing of five male figures depicted from the waist up. The men are in close proximity, appearing to be engaged in a conversation. The figure on the left wears a bowler hat and a coat, sporting a mustache and angular facial features. Next to him, two men are wearing military-style caps; they have beards and their expressions are partially obscured by the beards and shading. The central figure has distinct facial hair and a large mustache, and he is dressed in a uniform with noticeable buttons. He appears to be gesturing with his hand. The two figures on the right also wear hats and have long beards, with one seemingly looking at the central figure. The background is a beige-colored paper with printed text filling the right and left margins, detailing information about a play titled "L’Inspecteur Général 'REVIZOR'."

artworks.title: A Bas Le Progrès!; Mademoiselle Julie; Le Ménage Brésile
artworks.medium: 4-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a painting of a marching band procession. The scene depicts a group of individuals wearing blue coats and red hats, marching in formation. In the foreground, musicians play brass instruments such as the horn and tuba, leading the procession. The background shows the continuation of the marchers along a path edged by a building. To the left of the image, there is text listing a theatre program with titles such as "A Bas Le Progrès!", "Mademoiselle Julie", and "Le Ménage Brésilè". The text appears to frame the image as part of a theatrical playbill or advertisement. The artwork features colored pencil or crayon application, with a pointillist or stippling effect in its color. This is in the style of Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec.

artworks.title: A Bas Le Progrès!; Mademoiselle Julie; Le Ménage Brésile
artworks.medium: 4-color lithograph on laid paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: This painting features a marching band parade. The image shows a group of musicians in uniform, wearing bright blue coats and red hats, marching in formation. In the foreground, musicians are seen playing brass instruments enthusiastically. The composition captures the movement and energy of the parade as it travels along a street lined with simple structures. The use of bright colors and bold outlines creates a lively and somewhat festive atmosphere.

artworks.title: A Bas Le Progrès!
artworks.medium: 3-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a man with a rifle breaking a tool. The image features a man in a white shirt and blue trousers, breaking a wooden object with a rifle. The text around the image includes the phrase "A BAS LE PROGRÈS." The drawing has a soft, sepia-toned background, with the man's clothing color and the rifle in muted shades. The artist's signature and some additional text are present. The overall tone of the drawing conveys resistance or protest against advancement or change.

artworks.title: Theater Program for "Boubouroche" and "Valet de coeur (Jack of Hearts)"
artworks.medium: color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: The image shows an aerial view of a canal with a barge docked, buildings in the distance, and a bridge crossing over the canal. The scene is painted in bold brushstrokes with warm earth tones dominating the color palette. Two figures are walking on a path on the left, with a bridge and distant hills in the background. The image is framed by text, resembling a page from a theatrical program.

artworks.title: Theater Program for "Boubouroche" and "Valet de coeur (Jack of Hearts)"
artworks.medium: color lithograph on laid paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: This is a painting of a canal scene with a barge and two figures. There is a wooden barge with a red, green, and white painted pattern on its stern. In the foreground, two figures in dark clothing are on a yellow-colored surface. To the left, a bridge and other structures are in the background. The piece uses muted colors focusing on form and texture, with variations of color for depth. This is in the style of Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec.

artworks.title: Grand-Papa; Si c'était
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on wove paper
artworks.description: The image depicts an artistic pencil sketch showing three figures. Two figures are standing, while one is lying on the ground. The standing figure on the left is depicted with the upper half of the body, leaning forward slightly with arms crossed over a rounded abdomen. The facial features of this figure are simplistic with minimal detail, and the person appears to have short hair and wear a long, loose-fitting garment. The standing figure on the right is shown from head to toe with hands resting on their hips. This figure also has simplified facial features and appears to have short, wavy hair, wearing a loose garment and socks extending above the ankles. The third figure is lying on the ground in a reclining position, with a partially visible face showing closed eyes, positioned horizontally in relation to the standing figures. The person's clothing is undefined but suggests a garment suitable for lying down. The background is plain, indicating an illustration rather than a realistic setting. Accurate text elements on the left describe a theatrical performance titled "Grand-Papa," by Claude Berton, associated with 'Le Théâtre Libre,' listing the cast and other performance information for the 1894-1895 season.

artworks.title: La Belle au bois rêvant; Mariage d'argent; Ahasvère
artworks.medium: 5-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: The painting depicts individuals seated in a cafe or restaurant setting. Some men are reading newspapers at booths. The interior has red seating and yellow walls. There are pitchers and glasses on a table. A program for theatrical or musical events is on the right listing three performances and names of characters and performers. The style is similar to Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec's lively scenes of Parisian nightlife.

artworks.title: Le Devoir
artworks.medium: 4-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: The image depicts three men in a bar or pub setting. The first man wears a blue suit and hat, facing the bartender. The second man, the bartender, wears a sleeveless black vest, a white shirt, and has a mustache. The third man, leaning against the bar, wears a brown coat and a cap. The bar counter with bottles is visible in the background, along with pale yellow walls. The style suggests it is associated with Le Théatre-Libre's 1892-1893 season.

artworks.title: Le Devoir
artworks.medium: 4-color lithograph on laid paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: This is a painting of a bar scene with three individuals. The figures are depicted in a bar-like setting, with one leaning against the bar, another standing with a hand gesture, and a third seated. They are dressed in early 20th-century fashion. The bar counter has bottles and a glass. The background includes a shaded archway, and the color palette consists of greens, browns, and yellows. The style is sketchy and outlined, reminiscent of Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec.

artworks.title: Le Grappin; L'Affranchie
artworks.medium: 6-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a painting of a theatrical program poster. The image features a colorful and animated poster for a theatrical performance at "Le Théâtre Libre," featuring plays titled "Le Grappin" and "L'Affranchie." The design includes illustrations of two figures dressed in bright yellow outfits standing on the left side of the image, along with a stout character on the right wearing red shorts. Both are posed as if they are part of the theatrical narrative. The play titles and the names of various actors and roles are printed in a stylized font between the two groups of figures. In the lower right corner, two figures wearing red and black hats appear to be observing the event.

artworks.title: Le Grappin; L'Affranchie
artworks.medium: 6-color lithograph on laid paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: The image shows three individuals standing on a wooden platform. On the left, two women are dressed in matching yellow dresses with white trims and white shoes. The taller woman has dark hair styled in an updo and crossed arms, while the shorter woman has long, straight dark hair and rests her arm on the taller woman's hip. On the right, a muscular man stands confidently with his hands on his hips. He wears a red outfit resembling a singlet, white socks, and has a bald head with side hair and a prominent mustache. In the background, there is a green backdrop with a circus scene, including red and white striped balloons, a green tent, figures in winter attire, and a sandy or gravel path where two men in red caps and coats are partially visible.

artworks.title: Les Fossiles
artworks.medium: 6-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a painting of a coastal scene with spectators observing the sea. The composition consists of a group of figures seated on a sandy beach facing the sea, with three visible sailboats in the distance. The figures are outlined in bold, dark lines with contrasting blocks of colors. In the background, the horizon features a calm sea rendered in shades of turquoise and pale yellow, with a band of light yellow sky above. On the right side of the image, two figures walk hand-in-hand towards the sea. The left side of the image contains text detailing a theatre program titled "Les Fossiles" for "Le Théâtre Libre".

artworks.title: Les Tisserands
artworks.medium: 5-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of workers in an industrial setting. The image depicts several topless figures pushing carts filled with material, along a track beside a large mound. In the background, there are outlines of industrial buildings with smokestacks against an orange sky. The left side of the image contains a detailed listing resembling a playbill with names and roles, suggesting it may be related to a theatrical production titled "Les Tisserands." The scene is characterized by dark, heavily textured shading contrasting with highlights of color.

artworks.title: Dancing Nude and Advertisement for Eugène Verneau's "Estampes décoratives" [verso]
artworks.medium: transfer lithograph in brown on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a human figure. The image features a detailed sketch of a nude male figure in a dynamic pose, set against a swirling backdrop. The figure's body is muscular and well-defined, positioned as if stepping forward. There is a sense of energy in the curly hair and arches of the background elements. On the left side of the drawing, there is a vertical block of text about offerings by Eugène Verneau, a printer and publisher from Paris. The style of the drawing emphasizes form and posture.

artworks.title: Nell Horn
artworks.medium: 4-color lithograph with embossing (gaufrage) on wove paper
artworks.description: This image depicts a theater performance announcement featuring a silhouetted figure. The drawing shows a female figure with arms outstretched, rendered in a stippling or spray paint effect in red transitioning into yellow. The background includes text related to a theatrical performance titled "NELL HORN," a drama in four acts and six tableaux, in prose. The text also includes the name of the theater, "Le Théâtre Libre," the performance season of 1891-1892, and a performance date of Monday, May 25, 1891. Various roles and characters associated with the play are listed with names and descriptive titles for actors or personas, suggesting the image serves as a poster or playbill for a vintage theatrical production.

artworks.title: Mirages
artworks.medium: 5-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: This painting features a theater program illustration. The scene showcases audience members in the foreground observing performers on stage. The image is filled with vibrant and textured colors, with a section at the top left listing cast members and roles for a performance titled "Mirages." The audience is depicted in semi-profile, while the performers on stage are shown in dynamic poses against a green and yellow backdrop. An orchestra is illustrated in the lower right corner, contributing to the lively atmosphere of the theater setting. The artwork captures the essence of a late 19th-century theater experience and is stylistically reminiscent of Henri-Gabriel Ibels.

artworks.title: Mirages
artworks.medium: 5-color lithograph on Arches laid paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: This is a painting of a theater scene viewed from an elevated position. The composition features a view of a stage from behind an audience. The stage is populated by dancers dressed in white tutus, their poses suggesting movement as they perform. In the foreground, a few members of the audience are seen from behind, sitting in chairs that are arranged in a curved formation. The orchestra is visible to the right, with musicians playing their instruments, while the conductor energetically directs the performance. The colors used include green, yellow, and red, giving the scene a vibrant atmosphere. The style is reminiscent of Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, known for his depictions of Parisian nightlife and performance settings.

artworks.title: Ubu Roi
artworks.medium: photomechanical process in black on pink wove paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: The image shows bold, black lines and shapes on a tan background forming an abstract composition. In the scene, a large, round figure with a cone-shaped hat holding a scythe is looming over a smaller group of figures holding papers or books. The large figure also holds a bag labeled "5,000". Flames rise from a building with windows.

artworks.title: Ubu Roi
artworks.medium: photomechanical process in black on pink wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a theatrical advertisement. The image is an advertisement for a theatrical production titled "Ubu Roi." The composition features a combination of text and illustrative graphics on a poster. In the upper left, there is a block of text listing cast members and theatrical details. On the right side, a large figure is wielding a weapon above their head, opposite an ornamental plant and a structure in flames, with a sack marked "5,000" nearby. Below, two figures appear engaged in reading or discussion. The style is reminiscent of woodcut illustrations, with bold, simplistic forms and strong contrasts.

artworks.title: Ubu Roi
artworks.medium: photomechanical process in black on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a theatrical poster for "Ubu Roi" by Alfred Jarry. The artwork features a rotund figure with a triangular hat holding a sack and a sword, along with another figure pulling a cart, and a house on fire. The drawing is done in a monochrome style typical of poster art from the late 19th century. It contains a whimsical depiction of characters and abstract shapes, filled with text and symbols possibly referencing the absurdist themes of the play.

artworks.title: Ubu Roi; Petits Poèmes amorphes
artworks.medium: photomechanical process in green on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: The image contains abstract shapes and bold lines, creating a sense of movement. In the center is a large, angular shape with exaggerated features. Above it are jagged lines connecting to the text "THÉÂTRE DES PANTINS." Below, two face-like shapes are intertwined, with cartoonish and theatrical expressions. The composition uses dark strokes to outline the forms against a lighter background, resembling a poster for a theatrical performance.

artworks.title: Le Fils de l'abbesse; Le Fardeau de la liberté
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on wove paper
artworks.description: The image displays a flat perspective of a forest scene. The horizon is hidden by vertical tree trunks stretching from the foreground into the background. The art style features linear brushstrokes creating textures resembling bark and foliage. The color palette is monochromatic with varying shades of black on an off-white or yellowed background. The image is set against a printed publication background with text and a figure, possibly a woman, among the trees.
